q: Which comparison of aerobic and anaerobic respiration in human muscle is correct?
options: Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2, whereas aerobic respiration produces lactate, CO2 and water
Aerobic uses O2 and mitochondria (~30 ATP/glucose); anaerobic stays in the cytoplasm, makes lactate (2 ATP)
Anaerobic respiration yields more ATP per glucose than aerobic, but it releases that ATP more slowly
Aerobic respiration happens only in the cytoplasm, and anaerobic respiration happens only in mitochondria
explanation: Human anaerobic respiration = glycolysis + conversion of pyruvate to lactate, all in the cytoplasm, giving net 2 ATP per glucose and no CO2 (unlike yeast, which makes ethanol + CO2). Aerobic respiration continues pyruvate through the link reaction, Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria, yielding about 15 times more ATP per glucose.
